metadata.title: A Commons Beyond the Airlock
metadata.source_title: A Commons Beyond the Airlock — original fixture story

adaptation.rights_basis: Original fixture story authored for this project

interpretation.summary: A stranded habitat's allocation software mistakes an inherited census for a complete account of its residents. Maintenance workers use scarce power and recovered administrative evidence to challenge that authority.
interpretation.era: A failing orbital relay after the supply fleet withdrew
interpretation.technology: Repair drones, inductive tools, sealed habitats and ration algorithms
interpretation.supernatural_rules: No magic; energy and pressure obey physical constraints, and autonomous systems follow stale authority.
factions_and_cultures: Life support priorities require consent from the people they affect.
Technicians sign repairs with a visible audit trail and share spare parts by need.
interpretation.social_structures: A mutual-aid group challenges control of essential infrastructure.
interpretation.geography: sealed service corridors and abandoned hydroponics
conflicts: Reconfigure the oxygen scheduler so every resident has a share and a voice.
relationships: The protagonist owes a practical debt to the guide; both need the residents' trust.
interpretation.narrative_structure: Discover the excluded, recover their record, then open the institution to shared control.
interpretation.danger: Ordinary enforcers teach tactics before a stronger guardian.
interpretation.morality: Care does not justify ownership of another life.

creative_direction.world_bible: The Orison Relay is a sealed service corridors and abandoned hydroponics. A stranded habitat's allocation software mistakes an inherited census for a complete account of its residents. Maintenance workers use scarce power and recovered administrative evidence to challenge that authority. Technicians sign repairs with a visible audit trail and share spare parts by need. The central institution remains dangerous because a mobile enforcement chassis protecting a life-support schedule that omits the undocumented berths. The protagonist is a zero-gravity relay technician with a working relationship to a life-support coordinator; occupational tools and recovered records provide ways to change that institution.
creative_direction.gameplay_identity: Play a zero-gravity relay technician, recover contested records, use occupational tools or negotiate, and turn discoveries into institutional change.
creative_direction.originality_strategy: Independent original fixture story and cast; no external book adaptation.
creative_direction.main_narrative: Reconfigure the oxygen scheduler so every resident has a share and a voice.
side_narratives: Make discarded components useful to neighbors.
quality_criteria: Every quest changes a practical obligation
The final gate opens through shared knowledge, not arbitrary level gating

visual_style: Cool blue service decks, copper wires and diagnostic glyphs; ASCII is a terminal mode.
audio_direction: Soft relay clicks, air circulation, clipped alert tones instead of magical fanfares.

nodes.text: The bus holds the old census key. Bring it here and we can unlock the scheduler without venting the berths.
The people keeping this place alive have no place in its official record. If we disappear, its rulers will call the accounts balanced.
